title: THE DAY WREN WAS RIGHT
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: The closing story returns to an intimate civic scale and lets Wren be substantively right about the shape of the floating market's sanitation problem. The informal ledger already doing most of the work creates a strong reframing opportunity: Illuminara's contribution can be to prove the missing links and secure durable authority without appropriating the community's system. The outcome is concrete—a community-run sanitation scheme and lease—yet the two excluded families keep the success morally and operationally nontrivial.

Reframing adopted: the plan is not wrong because it is inefficient but because it models the market as a machine; Wren's objection is design input and the tie-book is already the sanitation system, failing in three places found by what it omits (Reed Row's Sunday gap, the single pump owner, and the absence of any outcome-based way to show the Order it works). Strongest rival cause (the tannery drain) is tested with a sealed prediction card and four stations; the compliance link is solved by measuring water rather than boats under Order 14 section 6(b). Wren is right on form and keeps a real disagreement over the ten-year term; the council, Gwil, Hesper, Odalys, Beck and Dross each keep a refusal. Costs left standing: Dross leaves unreconciled, Beck's tank is a patch, the lease is short.

THE DAY WREN WAS RIGHT has a sound frame (a floating market is already a sanitation system, and the compliance question is outcomes versus names), a live rival cause tested by a sealed prediction, a companion whose objection is design input, and refusals that survive (Dross leaves, Wren keeps her quarrel with the ten-year term). The weaknesses are all in the load-bearing mechanism, not the frame. The decisive legal route appears in scene four as a clause nobody mentioned before; the book's three holes are announced rather than found; and the central physical claim (a day of rest produces a tenfold spike) has no visible cause. Fix these and the solution reads as earned instead of convenient.

Revision after the Claude fallback self-review T02 (independent_peer_review false, so the criticism was taken as adversarial self-checking, not peer consensus). Frame kept: a working informal system versus a vessel-list law, Wren right on form, refusals that survive. Salvaged unchanged in substance: Wren's 'rumour with a rota', the sealed card, the live tannery rival with its upstream station left standing, Dross declining unconverted, Beck's tank as an admitted patch, Odalys refusing Illuminara the page. Small repairs: the four stations are now called four (scene three title), and the Mabuya/Gwil pump-owner inconsistency in the draft is resolved to Gwil Anand throughout. Outcome (rule 3a): Kettle keeps its twelve hundred households; Sunday discharge at Reed Row falls from 2300 to 310 and the outfall from 700 to 190, under the 200 standard; the Inspector certifies a community arrangement without opening the book; Illuminara's decisive contributions are the book-reading that finds the Sunday cause, the sealed-prediction test that separates it from the tannery, and the reading of section 6(b) as an outcomes route with an inspectable signer. Costs that remain: a ten-year lease, Dross's unreconciled exit, Beck's patch, seven refused strings, and Reed Row's own Sunday expense. Length is 2543 words by the counting rule, slightly above the 2500 guide; every scene carries a decision, so no cut was made.

T03 resolves all three ranked T02 requests without weakening the story's central frame. The equivalent-arrangement route is planted before the solution and Aldana's silence now has a liability reason; the Reed Row Sunday spike follows from small tanks, weekend visitors, the Friday carry and repeatedly repaired relief valves; and the sealed card fixes the outfall station and its two-hundred standard before sampling. The council decision now has a visible 31-to-7 tally, a recorded dissent and costs borne by Reed Row, while Dross, Beck, Odalys and Wren retain independent agency. No further priority revision is justified. The author may issue T05 as the final, preserving the verified source unless a purely editorial correction is necessary.

Final issued as the unchanged T03 text, as the independent peer review asked (no editorial correction needed, so no new content hash). Outcome (rule 3a): Kettle keeps its twelve hundred households; Sunday discharge at Reed Row falls from 2300 to 310 and the outfall from 700 to 190, under the 200 standard fixed on the sealed card; the Inspector certifies a community arrangement without opening the book; Illuminara's decisive contributions are reading the book for what it omits, the sealed-prediction test that separates the Sunday cause from the tannery, and the reading of section 6(b) as an outcomes route with an inspectable signer. Costs that remain: a ten-year lease Wren still calls a leash, Dross's unreconciled exit, Beck's patch, seven refused strings, Reed Row's own Sunday expense, and the ledger staying in Odalys's hands.

A floating market survives a deserved sanitation deadline because Illuminara treats Wren's objection as a better model, proves the Sunday leak with a sealed test, and builds an inspectable outcome around the community's own private tie-book without seizing it.
